objects.name: Chipkin Example B-SA
objects.note: the device itself; the instance is configurable with --deviceID. The stack rows are device-wide facts only the stack knows - the protocol version and revision it implements, the services and object types it was configured with, the live object list and address-binding table. The accepted rows are the stack's configured defaults for APDU limits, segmentation, system status and database revision; an application that answered them from its own constants could contradict the stack, so this example does not

objects.name: Bronze
objects.note: REAL, degrees Celsius; the temperature the simulated heating valve produces - it moves up to 1.0 C a second toward the winning Analog Output 1 setpoint (starts at 21.5)

objects.name: Emerald
objects.note: the simulated relay's feedback contact - takes the winning Binary Output 1 command within a second (starts inactive)

objects.name: Hot Pink
objects.note: 3 states: On, Off, Auto; the simulated drive's speed - takes the winning Multi-State Output 1 command within a second

objects.name: Chartreuse
objects.note: REAL setpoint, degrees Celsius, commandable via a 16-slot Priority_Array; Relinquish_Default 20.0; accepts 10.0 .. 30.0 (Min_Pres_Value / Max_Pres_Value), else value-out-of-range. Reliability reads no-fault-detected, or no-output while the simulated valve actuator is disconnected; the stack derives Status_Flags FAULT from it

objects.name: Fuchsia
objects.note: active/inactive relay, commandable via a 16-slot Priority_Array; Relinquish_Default inactive; a value other than 0/1 gets value-out-of-range

objects.name: Indigo
objects.note: speed state 1..3, commandable via a 16-slot Priority_Array; Relinquish_Default state 1; a state outside 1..3 gets value-out-of-range

objects.name: Vermilion
objects.note: BACnet/IP; Network_Type and Protocol_Level are set from BACnetStack_AddNetworkPortObject()'s arguments (IPv4, BACnet Application) at start-up, not a GetProperty callback like the object's other app-served rows; Changes_Pending is likewise computed and answered natively by the stack's Network Port object. Reliability has no fault condition this example detects, so it is accepted at the generic default (normal)
